evidence: Type assignment matches the ask in every file. Gates: render/authenticated_render and constraints/server_backed_local_application are binary (gates/*/judge.toml:23), as required for all_pass gates. Functional: all 16 criteria are binary, weighted 1.5-4.0 (e.g. wall_every_route:57, timer_changes:134, search_and_transcript:248, persistence:269); each is a pass/fail behaviour (wall leaks, timer deletion, stale-edit refusal, idempotent send) with explicit Fails-if wording, so likert would add no meaningful gradation. Polish: six binary criteria (polish/judge.toml:23-68) that are each an observable behaviour with a pass/fail condition: Enter/Shift+Enter, Escape cancels, delete asks to confirm, deep-link highlight persists ~10 s, transcript scrollWidth equals viewport at 390 px, and the refusal reason stays by the form. None of them grades craft or degree of quality. Visual: all four criteria (matter_sidebar, retention_marks, transcript_page, phone_chambers) are type='likert', points=5, with a described anchor at every level 5..0 (visual/judge.toml:28-33, 44-49, 60-65, 76-81), the same as the template's 0-5 anchor convention (template visual/judge.toml:20-33). visual/prompt.md:28-36 makes the anchored 0-5 integer scale authoritative over RewardKit's generic 1-5 hint, word for word as the template does. Per SKILL.md:65 and quality-checks.md:170, the internal workbook note (likert unused, binary+weighted) is a known false positive. The shipped format allows likert in scored dimensions (staged-task-contract.md:135). Adversarial probes: (a) Broken app that could pass: an app with polished craft but no unread counts would score 5 on matter_sidebar because of its absent-count carve-out (visual/judge.toml:27). The functional binary unread_and_new_messages_line (weight 1.5) still fails it, and only 0.2 of the reward mass is visual. The carve-out also protects a conforming app whose counts are already read, so this is a correct split between behaviour and craft, not a binary/likert defect. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: a matter list on its own phone or desktop screen rather than a sidebar is explicitly allowed (visual:27). A transcript laid out differently still meets transcript_page, whose anchors grade document-likeness, not a fixed layout, consistent with walls-and-retention.md:35's 'plain reading page'. Polish binaries accept either an in-page or a browser confirm dialog (polish:44). Neither probe exposes craft wrongly binarised or a pass/fail behaviour wrongly likert-graded. Observations (not defects): some intermediate anchors are terse, e.g. matter_sidebar 4 'clear with one weak selection state' and retention_marks 4 'clear with one weak mark'. They are still described per level, which this row requires. No configured judge run of the visual dimension exists on these bytes (raw-evidence-index scope: render/visual not covered), so actual likert spread is unmeasured. That belongs to rows 40/42 (discrimination/ranking), not to this row's format-fit criterion.
